name: the Russian Synodal Bible
title: Synodal (RUSV) against BHSA and Nestle 1904
notes: «В начале»: «В» → בְּ, «начале» → רֵאשִׁית. A dative such as «Господу» for לַיהוָה links to both לַ and יהוָה; a preposition the Russian supplies where the Hebrew has none stays unlinked.
Russian «и», «а», «но» link to וְ/καί when they render it; a supplied «и» stays unlinked. In Gen 1:1 «и» does not link to אֵת.

Possessives and object pronouns («его», «ее», «их», «свой», «мой», «твой», «ему», «тебе») link to the word carrying the suffix: «сына своего» → בְּנוֹ, «жену свою» → אִשְׁתּוֹ (Gen 4:1). «свой» agrees with any person. Subject pronouns of a verb ending link to the verb: «он сказал» → וַיֹּאמֶר.
Verb forms of two words link to the one original verb: «да будет» → יְהִי (Gen 1:3). «смертью умрешь» for מוֹת תָּמוּת: «смертью» → מוֹת, «умрешь» → תָּמוּת.

Greek δέ is rendered by «же», «а», «но», «и»: link them to it; an emphatic «же» that renders no word stays unlinked. A pronoun or demonstrative for the Greek article links to the article (ἡ δέ «Она же», Mt 14:8).
In אֲדֹנָי יְהוִה the Synodal writes «Владыка Господь» or «Господь Бог»: the first word renders אֲדֹנָי, the second יְהוִה.

The Synodal translation follows the Septuagint in places: words or clauses it has from the Greek Old Testament (often printed in brackets) have no Hebrew counterpart and stay unlinked; a Hebrew word it renders after the Septuagint's reading is still its counterpart when the meaning corresponds.
The Synodal New Testament follows the Received Text, so a Russian word with no Nestle 1904 counterpart is not an error: leave it unlinked, and do not link it to another Nestle word.

The corpus numbers this text's chapters as the English Bibles do, but psalm titles are part of verse 1 here while the Hebrew numbers the title as a verse of its own; the frame line shows which Hebrew verses each verse maps to, and a link into the next Hebrew verse there is not a link to the wrong verse.
